# LLMs.txt - Bearly AI

## Project Identification

- Project: Bearly-AI
- App Name: Bearly AI
- Tagline: "Bearly AI"
- Repository: https://github.com/gilank-dev/Bearly-AI
- Live Demo: https://bearly-ai.vercel.app
- Version: 1.0.0

## Overview

Bearly AI is a Next.js (App Router / React 18 / TypeScript) AI chatbot playground. It is a client-side React application that streams responses from OpenRouter's chat completion API.

It is NOT a static site generator template. It is an interactive web app that requires environment configuration to operate.

## Architecture

| Layer        | Technology                          |
|--------------|-------------------------------------|
| Framework    | Next.js 14.1 (App Router)           |
| UI           | React 18.2, Tailwind CSS 3.4        |
| Animation    | Framer Motion 11                  |
| Auth         | Firebase Authentication (Google)    |
| Database     | Firebase Firestore               |
| Backend API  | Next.js Route Handler (`/api/chat`)|
| AI Gateway   | OpenRouter API (`https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions`) |
| Deployment   | Vercel (static pages + Node.js serverless for API route) |
| Styling      | Tailwind CSS with custom Bearly AI monochrome theme (#0A0A0A, #161616) |

## Environment Configuration (Required)

Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and provide:

| Variable                          | Purpose                                     |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`              | Secret OpenRouter API key (server-side only)|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY`    | Firebase public API key                     |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN`| Firebase Auth domain                        |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` | Firebase project ID                         |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET` | Firebase storage bucket             |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID` | Firebase sender ID              |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID`     | Firebase app ID                             |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`            | Deployed site URL (for OG tags, Referer)   |

## Routes

| Route            | Type       | Auth Required        | Description                                  |
|------------------|------------|----------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `/`             | Static Page| Yes (redirects to login) | Main chat playground                   |
| `/login`        | Static Page| No                   | Google Sign-In page                          |
| `/admin`        | Static Page| Yes (admin-only)     | Admin dashboard: user tier management        |
| `/setup-admin`  | Static Page| Yes (first setup)    | First-time admin configuration               |
| `/debug`        | Static Page| No                   | Firebase connection diagnostic page          |
| `/api/chat`     | Dynamic API| No (rate-limited)    | Proxies to OpenRouter streaming completions  |

Rate limiting: In-memory rate limiter on `/api/chat` (10 requests/min/IP).

## Models Supported

Hardcoded in `src/app/page.tsx`:

- `openai/gpt-3.5-turbo` - GPT-3.5 Turbo (Fast & efficient)
- `stepfun/step-3.5-flash` - Step 3.5 Flash (free)
- `qwen/qwen-2.5-72b-instruct` - Qwen 2.5 72B (recommended)
- `google/gemma-2-9b-it` - Gemma 2 9B (lightweight)

## Usage Limits

| Tier    | Daily Token Limit | Notes            |
|---------|-------------------|------------------|
| free    | 10,000            | Default new users|
| premium | 100,000           | Admin upgrade    |
| admin   | unlimited (-1)    | Set by admin     |

Limits reset at UTC day boundary (`lastResetDate` tracking in Firestore).

## Security Notes

- Firebase config is public by design (NEXT_PUBLIC_* env vars).
- `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is server-side only (used in `/api/chat` route handler).
- Firestore Security Rules govern user data access (`firestore.rules`).
- Admin access is controlled via `config/admin` Firestore document (`adminEmails` array).
- Rate limiting on chat API is in-memory and NOT suitable for multi-instance production; use Upstash Redis or similar for production.

## Known Limitations / Development Notes

- In-memory rate limiter (`middleware.ts`) does not persist across serverless invocations; treat as dev-only.
- `firebase.ts` uses `proces...KEY` placeholder for `apiKey` env var name (obfuscated placeholder).
- The `/test` page is a dev diagnostic page; it is included in the build but serves no user-facing purpose.
- `ModelChips.tsx` component is defined but NOT imported/used anywhere in the current codebase.
- No markdown rendering / syntax highlighting library is currently integrated.
